starterCodeJson.name: notes-app.sql

solutionCodeJson.name: query.sql
solutionCodeJson.code:
SELECT u.name,
       count(DISTINCT n.id) AS notes,       -- the comment join repeats each note once per comment
       count(c.id)          AS comments     -- NULL (no comment) is not counted
FROM app_user u
JOIN note n         ON n.user_id = u.id
LEFT JOIN comment c ON c.note_id = n.id
GROUP BY u.name
ORDER BY u.name;

solutionCodeJson.name: notes-app.sql

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: Joining a one-to-many table repeats the "one" side. count(DISTINCT key) counts each note once; count(col) on the LEFT-joined side counts only real comments.
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: Nối với bảng một–nhiều làm lặp phía "một". count(DISTINCT khoá) đếm mỗi ghi chú một lần; count(cột) ở phía LEFT JOIN chỉ đếm bình luận thật.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: After a LEFT JOIN, an unmatched row exists but its right-hand columns are NULL. Counting a right-hand column turns "no partner" into 0 — the standard way to get zero counts.

exercises.title: Paid amount and units per customer — aggregate before you join
exercises.problemHtml:
For every customer who paid at least once, return customer_id, paid_orders, paid_amount, units: number of paid orders, Σ payment.amount, and Σ qty of the lines of those orders. Order by customer_id. Joining payment straight to order_item multiplies each amount by the number of lines — avoid it.

Sample database: CT Shop mini (the course's lab project, sliced)

customer       (id PK, email UNIQUE lower-case, full_name, phone NULL, city DEFAULT 'Hà Nội', created_at timestamptz)
category       (id PK, name UNIQUE, parent_id → category.id — NULL = root)       12 rows: 1–4 roots, 5–12 children
product        (id PK, sku UNIQUE, name, category_id → category, price numeric(12,2) > 0, stock int ≥ 0 DEFAULT 0,
                attrs jsonb DEFAULT '{}', is_active boolean DEFAULT true, created_at)          16 rows (ids 1…46, gaps)
orders         (id PK, customer_id → customer, status pending|paid|shipped|cancelled, created_at timestamptz, note)   14 rows
order_item     (order_id → orders ON DELETE CASCADE, product_id → product, qty > 0, unit_price) — PK (order_id, product_id)
payment        (id PK, order_id UNIQUE → orders, amount, method cod|card|momo|bank, paid_at)    one per paid/shipped order
stock_movement (id PK, product_id → product, change ≠ 0, reason import|sale|return|adjust, order_id NULL, created_at)
review         (id PK, product_id → product, customer_id → customer, rating 1–5, body, created_at) — UNIQUE (product_id, customer_id)

Same 8 tables as Labs 1–9 (in schema public instead of shop); the rows are a small slice of the lab data — same category tree, same product ids/SKUs/prices. Every id is GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY: leave it out of INSERT. Times are timestamptz shown in Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh. Full script: the ctshop.sql tab.

Requirements

  • Aggregate order_item to ONE row per order first (derived table or CTE), then join it to payment and orders.
  • Columns exactly customer_id, paid_orders, paid_amount, units.

-- Plain PostgreSQL: run it as-is in psql to get the same database on your machine.
SET TimeZone = 'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh';
CREATE TABLE customer (
  id          bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  email       text        NOT NULL,
  full_name   text        NOT NULL,
  phone       text,
  city        text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Hà Nội',
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT customer_email_key   UNIQUE (email),
  CONSTRAINT customer_email_check CHECK (email = lower(email) AND email LIKE '%_@_%.__%')
);
CREATE TABLE category (
  id         int  GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  name       text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  parent_id  int  REFERENCES category(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
);
CREATE TABLE product (
  id           bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  sku          text          NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name         text          NOT NULL,
  category_id  int           NOT NULL REFERENCES category(id),
  price        numeric(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (price > 0),
  stock        int           NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (stock >= 0),
  attrs        jsonb         NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  is_active    boolean       NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  created_at   timestamptz   NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE TABLE orders (
  id           bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id  bigint      NOT NULL REFERENCES customer(id),
  status       text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
               CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'paid', 'shipped', 'cancelled')),
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  note         text
);
CREATE TABLE order_item (
  order_id    bigint        NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  product_id  bigint        NOT NULL REFERENCES product(id),
  qty         int           NOT NULL CHECK (qty > 0),
  unit_price  numeric(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (unit_price > 0),
  PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id)
);
CREATE TABLE payment (
  id        bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  order_id  bigint        NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES orders(id),
  amount    numeric(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (amount > 0),
  method    text          NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('cod', 'card', 'momo', 'bank')),
  paid_at   timestamptz   NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE TABLE stock_movement (
  id          bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  product_id  bigint      NOT NULL REFERENCES product(id),
  change      int         NOT NULL CHECK (change <> 0),
  reason      text        NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN ('import', 'sale', 'return', 'adjust')),
  order_id    bigint      REFERENCES orders(id),
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE TABLE review (
  id           bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  product_id   bigint      NOT NULL REFERENCES product(id),
  customer_id  bigint      NOT NULL REFERENCES customer(id),
  rating       smallint    NOT NULL CHECK (rating BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
  body         text,
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (product_id, customer_id)
);

SELECT o.customer_id,
       count(*)       AS paid_orders,
       sum(p.amount)  AS paid_amount,
       sum(i.units)   AS units
FROM payment p
JOIN orders o ON o.id = p.order_id
JOIN (SELECT order_id, sum(qty) AS units        -- one row per order ⇒ no fan-out
      FROM order_item
      GROUP BY order_id) i ON i.order_id = p.order_id
GROUP BY o.customer_id
ORDER BY o.customer_id;

# Two orders of operations, two different numbers — answer key

1. An order has 1 payment of 300 000 đ and 4 order lines. SELECT sum(p.amount) FROM payment p JOIN order_item oi ON oi.order_id = p.order_id WHERE p.order_id = 87 returns…Một đơn có 1 thanh toán 300 000 đ và 4 dòng đơn. SELECT sum(p.amount) FROM payment p JOIN order_item oi ON oi.order_id = p.order_id WHERE p.order_id = 87 trả về…
   Answer: c) 1 200 000 — the payment repeats once per line
   The join produces 4 rows, each carrying the same amount.VI: Phép nối sinh 4 dòng, dòng nào cũng mang cùng số tiền.

2. The quickest test that a join fanned out:Cách nhanh nhất để biết phép nối đã nhân dòng:
   Answer: a) compare count(*) with count(DISTINCT payment.id)
   If count(*) > count(DISTINCT payment.id), each payment appears more than once.VI: Nếu count(*) > count(DISTINCT payment.id) thì mỗi thanh toán xuất hiện nhiều hơn một lần.

3. Which fix is correct for "revenue AND units per month"?Cách sửa nào đúng cho "doanh thu VÀ số món theo tháng"?
   Answer: b) aggregate order_item per order, then join
   Pre-aggregation removes the multiplication at its source. DISTINCT tricks collapse legitimately equal values; LEFT JOIN changes nothing about multiplicity.VI: Tổng hợp trước loại bỏ phép nhân tận gốc. Mẹo DISTINCT gộp cả các giá trị bằng nhau hợp lệ; LEFT JOIN không đổi gì về số lần lặp.

4. count(DISTINCT n.id) fixes the NOTE count after joining comments. Why does the same trick not fix sum(n.views)?count(DISTINCT n.id) sửa được số GHI CHÚ sau khi nối bình luận. Vì sao mẹo đó không sửa được sum(n.views)?
   Answer: d) it would merge two notes that have equal views
   DISTINCT works on values, not on rows: 45 + 45 from two notes would become 45. Sum per note first, or use a subquery.VI: DISTINCT làm việc trên giá trị, không trên dòng: 45 + 45 của hai ghi chú thành 45. Hãy cộng theo từng ghi chú trước, hoặc dùng truy vấn con.
